newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower, LME stock build expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower, LME stock build expected.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended lower Monday along with a weak LME copper market, with a further large rise LME warehouse copper stocks expected Tuesday.

"We saw some weakness ahead of LME stock data Tuesday, as another large build is expected, but the market is still caught in a range, supported by consumer hedge buying at lows, and capped by trade selling at highs," E.D. & F. Mann New York trader Fred Demler said.
COMEX March copper ended down 1.30 cents at 102.50 cents a lb after trading from 104.00 to 101.70 cents.
LME copper stocks jumped 26,100 tonnes Friday to 191,750 tonnes.

The prompt market remains tight, helped by tension between an alleged Far East trade house with a large short position and a European merchant looking to take delivery on a large long position, traders said.
But longer term, the supply/demand balance is seen moving into surplus later this year.

The COMEX March/May spread slipped to 2.60 cents a lb from 3.25 cents Friday, and 3.85 cents Jan 23, while in London the LME cash-to-three month spread edged down to $221.00 a tonne from $232.00 Friday.
Overall the uptrend in copper prices over the past three months remain intact though, analysts said.
"The range in copper should be defined as 100.40 to 105.80 cents, with longs probably safe buying 100.50 and risking to 99.15 cents on a close basis," CRB analyst Terry Roggensack said.

CFTC's Commitments of Traders data for the period ended Jan 28, released late Friday, showed little change in net long position of non-commercials (commodity funds), which remained around 11,000 contracts over the two week period.
Non-reportable positions or small traders also remained net long 10,091 contracts, analysts noted.
